subject: Operator key custody options for private deploy — feasibility and audit flow

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@helixbio.com>

Cc: infra-team@helixbio.com, legal@helixbio.com
Date: 2027-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operator key custody & audit process for private deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough — Helix is excited to move forward with a VPC private deployment of Redwood for our internal R&D inference workloads. Before we sign the order form, Legal has a couple of non-standard asks around operator key custody and an audit pathway we wanted to validate with you: 

1) We want an option where Helix holds the primary encryption keys in our HSM and Redwood operators are never able to export them. Is that possible for the on‑prem package or VPC option?

2) If Redwood needs to perform emergency maintenance requiring operator access, we need an auditable mechanism (time-boxed key‑escrow or sealed key release) with tamper-evident logs and a notification/approval flow to Helix security.

3) Compliance: we will need an evidence package (audit log export, operator session traces, and a signed statement of access scope) to satisfy internal auditors and potentially a SOC2 reviewer. Please call out what you can commit to contractually vs what would be an operational playbook item.

I've attached a short doc summarizing the asks and a redline placeholder from our legal team. Can you confirm feasibility and a recommended path (preferred: Helix-managed keys; fallback: Redwood sealed-escrow with HSM + attestation)?

Appreciate a quick read — we are aiming for sign-off by the end of next week.

Best,
Elena Rodriguez
Head of IT Security, Helix Bio

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the doc. High level: we support both patterns you described but they have different contract and operational implications. Quick bullets below; attaching a short internal brief that maps MSA / Order Form redline recommendations to an implementation path. Happy to hop on a 30‑minute sync if that helps.

- Helix-managed keys (preferred): feasible for VPC/private deployments. In this pattern Redwood runs inference nodes but all disk and model keys are wrapped by your KMS/HSM. Redwood operators do not receive unwrapped keys. Contractually this typically maps to a "customer KMS" clause + limitations on remote troubleshooting that we capture in an MSA addendum.

- Sealed-escrow (fallback): Redwood can implement a sealed-key release via HSM-backed escrow where a key is only unsealed after multi-party approval (Redwood + Helix security). This requires an escrow attestation addendum and SLA for release windows. Operationally we also provide immutable audit trails for the unseal event.

- Emergency maintenance: we can offer a time-limited access window with recorded session replay, signed audit exports, and a one-time cryptographic attestation. We recommend gating this behind an Order Form appendix that defines escalation, approvers, and evidence deliverables.

Next steps proposed:
1) Legal redline of the MSA addendum focused on key custody (I'll attach our recommended language).
2) Ops/infra sync to validate the HSM integration work and estimate timeline (cc: Sergio).
3) Draft of the audit/evidence checklist so your SOC2 reviewer can preview it.

I've attached "Key-Custody-Options-brief.pdf" and a placeholder redline (redlines_MSA_v3.docx).

—So

Elena / team — looping in Redwood Legal for the contract-level items and clarifying a few redline positions we expect to see. I captured these as proposed MSA addendum clauses; paste below for quick review.

----- Proposed language (summary) -----
1) Customer KMS clause: "Customer shall retain sole ownership and control over encryption keys used to protect Customer Data; Redwood personnel shall not have any ability to extract unencrypted keys or plaintext model data. Redwood will support use of Customer-managed HSMs or KMS endpoints in the deployment region."

2) Sealed Escrow release (optional fallback): "In the event of emergency maintenance where Customer-managed keys cannot be used to preserve availability, Customer and Redwood shall execute a sealed-escrow unseal protocol. Unsealing requires dual approval: (a) a named Helix approver, and (b) a Redwood security officer. Unseal events will be cryptographically signed and an evidence package (unseal artifact, session logs, and attestations) will be delivered to Customer within 24 hours."

3) Audit evidence & retention: "Redwood will deliver, on request and subject to agreed SLAs, immutable audit exports for operator sessions, unseal events, and relevant system-level logs for a retention period of X months (to be negotiated)."

4) Limited troubleshooting carve: "Where Customer-managed keys prevent Redwood from performing routine debugging, Redwood may request a temporary assisted access path under the sealed-escrow process; any such access requires prior approval per the sealed-escrow clause."

----- Questions for Helix legal -----
- For the sealed-escrow path, can Helix nominate 2 approvers (primary + backup) and accept a 24-hour SLA for evidence delivery?
- Is there any regulatory constraint (export control, cross-border keys) we should be aware of given Helix's EU collaborators? If yes, we will map region constraints into the Order Form.

Operational note (cc: Sergio): we'll need to validate whether the Helix HSM can be reached over a private peering link or if a fully isolated on-prem HSM is required — this changes deployment cadence. Sergio, can you estimate the integration work once Helix confirms HSM model / CA bundle?

I'll let the legal redline proceed; Soojin — happy to join the sync with Helix security next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik & Soojin — this is very helpful. A few quick confirmations from Helix Legal:

- We can nominate two approvers for sealed-escrow (primary + backup). We will aim for a 24-hour evidence SLA but need Redwood to commit to the same delivery window in the Order Form appendix.
- Regarding cross-border constraints: our primary HSM will be hosted in the US region; we do have collaborators in EU but will not share unwrapped keys across borders. Please include a geography clause limiting any key export or unseal to the deployment region.

Operational ask: can Redwood provide a sample audit export (anonymized) so our SOC2 reviewer can confirm log schema and retention fields? If you can share an example within 48 hours that would keep our timeline on track.

If we can get the MSA addendum redline and the sample audit export this week, procurement and legal will circulate the order form for signature next Monday.

Elena
